scope: source-bound document-stated procedural effects and motion/request boundaries; no officer, incident, lawsuit merits, settlement amount, or unqualified current-status claims

proof_atoms.matter_label: United States v. Town of Colorado City (D. Ariz.)
proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked order header shows Document 1229 filed July 2, 2025; the order grants the joint motion to terminate the injunction, terminates the injunction, excuses the monitor, and dismisses the matter with prejudice.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later docket entry, appeal, modification, or corrected DOJ link changes the effect.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: This atom records what the order states as a document event. It does not assert that no later event occurred.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked order and reasons resolves pending motions by denying immediate termination of the consent decree and approving entry into a sustainment plan period.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later sustainment order, termination order, appeal, or docket update changes the procedural posture.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: Sustainment is not termination; this atom blocks any display that says the decree ended.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked closing letter is dated April 24, 2026 and states that DOJ is closing its investigation of the Ville Platte Police Department, while cautioning that the decision is not a general endorsement of all policies and practices.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later DOJ letter, court filing, or source-page correction changes the closure signal.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: An investigation closure signal is not an exoneration of all conduct and does not erase findings, agreements, or reports.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked closing letter is dated February 7, 2025 and states that, based on compliance assessments, the agreement is terminated and DOJ’s investigation is closed.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later DOJ letter, settlement modification, source-page correction, or local record changes the closure signal.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: A DOJ closing letter is a source-bounded procedural event, not a general present-tense guarantee of agency practice.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked order header shows Case 0:25-cv-00048, Doc. 64, filed May 27, 2025; the order grants the United States’ motion to dismiss and dismisses the matter with prejudice, while treating related motions as moot.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later docket entry, appeal, correction, or renewed matter changes the procedural history.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: Dismissal of the federal action does not erase the existence of the prior findings report, complaint, consent decree text, or public controversy.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked order header shows Case 2:16-cv-01731, Document 360, filed May 17, 2024; the order grants partial termination for specified decree paragraphs and states that remaining subject-matter areas continue in effect.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later order fully terminates, modifies, or reopens the decree; source page is updated; docket disagrees.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: Partial termination cannot be displayed as full closure.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked order header shows Case 1:14-cv-01025, Document 1103, filed May 12, 2025; the order grants the joint motion for termination and dismisses the matter with prejudice.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: later docket entry, appeal, correction, or renewed matter changes the procedural history.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: The terminal order atom is not a broad factual claim that the department has no remaining accountability issues.

proof_atoms.matter_label: Louisville Metro Police Department and Louisville/Jefferson County Metro Government
proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked motion asks the court to dismiss the case with prejudice and to hold proceedings in abeyance, but the accessioned document is a motion rather than an order.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: court order resolves the motion or a docket check shows a different procedural posture.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: Motion-request atom explicitly prevents promotion to a dismissal claim.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked joint motion requests termination of the court-approved settlement agreement; paired order accession is required before the requested effect can be treated as ordered.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: paired court order contradicts or modifies the requested effect.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: The motion is useful for timeline ordering, not for status promotion by itself.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked Seattle motion asks the court to terminate the consent decree, but this accessioned document is a motion and not the court’s order.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: order on motion, docket update, or source-page correction.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: The motion-to-order distinction remains active even when DOJ’s page labels the row closed.

proof_atoms.document_effect_statement: The DOJ-linked United States response supports termination of the consent decree and dismissal with prejudice, but the response is not itself a termination order.
proof_atoms.rollback_trigger: court order on motion, subsequent docket entry, or source-page correction.
proof_atoms.nonclaim: A party response, even from DOJ, is not a court order.
